what: 72-label batch driven through the real batch UI, past the 60-row point where the bold measurement pass becomes opt-in. Run after the 2026-08-13 UI changes (shared verdict summary, relocated batch decisions, rebuilt bold spot-check crop), because the standing 250-row evidence predates all of them.
how: Six copies of the twelve bundled sample applications, each under its own filename, assembled in the browser and dropped on the batch dropzone as a CSV + 72 image files. Same client path as a real drop: per-image deskew, object URLs, filename pairing, streaming table.

check_pass.note: concurrency 8; per-label figure is wall-clock/labels, not per-request latency. The browser pane was not displayed, which suspends the renderer between interactions, so 56.8s is ACTIVE processing time as measured by the page, not wall time on a foregrounded tab.

opt_in_bold_pass.note: Counts move while the pass runs: a row still being measured sits in Matched and re-files to Needs review if the measurement comes back inconclusive. The settled figures are the ones recorded here — an early read at 10s showed 49 matched and 1 outstanding, which was optimistic by 16 rows. The settle time carries the same caveat as the check pass: active time, not wall time.

bold_spot_check_strip.note: Before 2026-08-13 a card whose warning band was missing rendered no image at all, only the text 'couldn't locate the warning — open the row'. 11 of 17 here would have been blank. The fallback crop says in words that it is guessing.

also_exercised: count-carrying filter chips tracking the gate as it settles
note_2026_08_14: The settle figures imply ~31 rows/min through ONE pre-pool worker, which contradicts ocr-pool.json's 11.9 rows/min through four pooled workers; both runs were measured with the browser pane hidden (renderer throttled), so neither rate is trustworthy. Also: this file's eligible_rows (56) and the 250-row files' 208/210 are different sessions — the counts move because one gate signal is a fresh model judgement per run.
